name: Omaha
tagline: Warren Buffett's Hometown, Incredible Steakhouses, and a Thriving Arts Scene
description: Omaha is proof that a low cost of living and a high quality of life are not mutually exclusive. Warren Buffett chose to stay here for a reason: the city offers exceptional value, a surprisingly sophisticated dining and arts scene, and a strong sense of community. Omaha's Old Market district is packed with galleries, restaurants, and live music, while the Henry Doorly Zoo is consistently ranked among the world's best. Housing is remarkably affordable, the steak is legendary, and a growing tech and startup scene gives the city a forward-looking energy that defies Midwestern stereotypes.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate to High – safe suburbs with typical urban core variability
quickFacts.climate: Continental with hot summers, cold winters, and dramatic seasonal changes

housing.description: Modest studio or older 1BR in Benson, the Dundee/Hanscom fringe, or an Aksarben edge

dining.description: Occasional cheap eats; food is overwhelmingly cooked at home

healthcare.description: A subsidized ACA Silver plan, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; Nebraska's unsubsidized prices are among the nation's highest, so losing the subsidy is unusually costly here. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car — Omaha auto insurance is high by US standards (full coverage ~$157/mo) — plus gas and upkeep; transit is too weak to rely on

entertainment.description: Parks, the riverfront, Old Market wandering, and Omaha's cheap-culture calendar

1M.lifestyle: A frugal but genuinely livable Omaha life anchored in an older Benson or Dundee-fringe apartment, home cooking, and free riverfront and park culture. Housing plus a subsidized health premium alone absorb the bulk of the budget — the classic US mid-metro squeeze — and a paid-off used car is a non-negotiable line because transit is thin. Winters put a real number on the utility line. Comfortable within its limits, with little discretionary slack.

housing.description: A proper 1BR in a desirable area — Benson proper, Midtown, or an entry Aksarben Village unit

dining.description: Out a few times a week at casual spots

healthcare.description: Subsidized ACA plan, MAGI managed under the cliff

transportation.description: A newer used car on full coverage at Omaha rates, plus gas and upkeep

2M.lifestyle: An unshowy, secure Omaha routine in a nice 1BR in Benson or Midtown, eating out a few nights a week, with a dependable car on full coverage. Health coverage stays subsidized by keeping income under the cliff. The tier that trades scarcity for stability without stretching.

housing.description: A quality 1BR in a walkable, sought-after pocket — Dundee, Blackstone/Midtown Crossing, Downtown, or a newer Aksarben Village build

dining.description: Several restaurant meals a week across Omaha's improving food scene

healthcare.description: Priced at the edge of the subsidy cutoff and padded — a richer plan while subsidized, or Silver plus meaningful out-of-pocket, to absorb the risk a drawdown pushes income over the subsidy cutoff into Nebraska's steep unsubsidized band

transportation.description: A comfortable car, full coverage, ample driving budget

entertainment.description: A real leisure and travel-seed budget, memberships, events

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, financially-independent Omaha life in a walkable Dundee or Midtown Crossing 1BR, dining out several times a week with a genuine travel budget. Healthcare is the swing variable — the line is intentionally padded because the ACA subsidy cutoff is unforgiving in Nebraska, one of the higher-premium states on the individual market. Everyday needs are fully covered; the constraint is discretionary scale, not comfort.

housing.description: A high-end 2BR or junior-2BR in a luxury building — top Aksarben Village stock, Midtown Crossing, or a Downtown high-rise

healthcare.description: Fully unsubsidized (MAGI over the cliff) — an age-rated 45–55 plan on Nebraska's high-average individual market (~$1,250; avg-silver $918 age-40 aged up), materially higher than a comparable Ohio figure

transportation.description: A premium vehicle, full coverage, generous fuel/rideshare

domesticHelp.description: Roughly biweekly housekeeping at Omaha rates (~$140/visit)

5M.lifestyle: An affluent Omaha lifestyle in a luxury Aksarben Village or Downtown high-rise apartment, with frequent fine dining, a premium car, and regular housekeeping help. Because income now sits above the ACA cliff, the health line jumps to Nebraska's full unsubsidized price — a notably heavier line than in lower-premium states. Real travel and discretionary budgets appear here without ostentation.

housing.description: The top of Omaha's rental market — a Downtown penthouse-tier unit or a high-end single-family rental in Regency, Happy Hollow, or Fairacres (rental stock at this level is thin — see confidence)

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized domestic plan (Gold or Platinum) plus a concierge or direct-primary-care membership, priced for ages 45-55 and reflecting Nebraska's higher unsubsidized market. This is a US domestic setup, not an international expat plan.

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus on-demand rideshare/driver

domesticHelp.description: Roughly weekly housekeeping plus occasional additional help/errands

luxuryExtras.description: Broad discretionary — travel, clubs, hobbies, indulgences

10M.lifestyle: The ceiling of what money buys in a mid-cost Midwest metro — a penthouse-tier or high-end Fairacres/Regency residence, daily fine dining, a luxury car with a driver when wanted, and full domestic help. Even at the top the health line stays fully unsubsidized and runs higher than an equivalent Ohio budget, because Nebraska's individual market is among the higher-premium states. At roughly $177k/year it is unambiguously lavish.
